ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, the line $y=-\frac{1}{2}x+b$ intersects the $x$-axis at point $A$ and the $y$-axis at point $B$, and intersects the graph of the function $y=kx$ at point $M(1, 2)$. Point $C$ is on the line segment $MA$, and a perpendicular line to the $x$-axis is drawn through point $C$, intersecting the graph of the function $y=kx$ at point $D$. If $2CD=OB$, find the coordinates of point $C$.
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} According to the problem,\\
$\because b=\frac{5}{2}$,\\
$\therefore OB= b=\frac{5}{2}$,\\
$\because 2CD=OB$,\\
$\therefore CD=\frac{1}{2}OB=\frac{1}{2}\times \frac{5}{2}=\frac{5}{4}$,\\
$\because$ point C is on the line $y=-\frac{1}{2}x+\frac{5}{2}$,\\
$-\frac{1}{2}x+\frac{5}{2}=\frac{5}{4}$,\\
Solving this, we get $x=\frac{5}{2}$,\\
The coordinates of point C are $\boxed{\left(\frac{5}{2}, \frac{5}{4}\right)}$.

Point $C$ is on the line segment $MA$, and a perpendicular line to the $x$-axis is drawn through point $C$, intersecting the graph of the function $y=kx$ at point $D$. If $2CD=OB$, find the coordinates of point $C$.
raw_record.answer:
\textbf{Solution:} According to the problem,\\
$\because b=\frac{5}{2}$,\\
$\therefore OB=b=\frac{5}{2}$,\\
$\because 2CD=OB$,\\
$\therefore CD=\frac{1}{2}OB=\frac{1}{2}\times\frac{5}{2}=\frac{5}{4}$,\\
$\because$ point C is on the line $y=-\frac{1}{2}x+\frac{5}{2}$,\\
$-\frac{1}{2}x+\frac{5}{2}=\frac{5}{4}$,\\
Solving this, we get $x=\frac{5}{2}$,\\
The coordinates of point C are $\boxed{\left(\frac{5}{2},\frac{5}{4}\right)}$.
